claims.claim: Author migrated blog from Hugo to Astro after years of good performance with Hugo
claims.quote: After years of good performance with Hugo, I decided to migrate my blog to Astro

claims.claim: Three key reasons for migration: flexibility, familiar syntax (JavaScript/TypeScript), and ease of getting started
claims.quote: flexibility, the familiar syntax and programming language (JavaScript/TypeScript), and how easy it is to get started

claims.claim: Author used Astro for small projects like Demo Time before the main migration
claims.quote: already used Astro a couple of times for some small projects (like Demo Time)

claims.claim: Astro developer experience is incredibly smooth
claims.quote: The developer experience with Astro is incredibly smooth

claims.claim: Astro enables easy React integration with components
claims.quote: I can make use of React in a relatively easy way

claims.claim: In Hugo, author used webpack for React search functionality
claims.quote: hooked everything up with webpack, but it still used a version that depended on Node.js 16

claims.claim: Previous migration from WordPress to Hugo occurred in 2019
claims.quote: In 2019, I migrated my blog from WordPress to Hugo to go fully static

claims.claim: Hugo worked flawlessly since 2019
claims.quote: Since 2019, it worked flawlessly

claims.claim: Blog content is stored in separate repository with Git submodules
claims.quote: my blog content lives in a separate repository that I include in my website via a Git submodule

claims.claim: Author has over 500 blog posts requiring conversion
claims.quote: As I have over 500 blog posts

claims.claim: Created Remark plugins to convert shortcodes and partials to components
claims.quote: created a couple of Remark plugins to convert the shortcodes/partials to Astro components

claims.claim: Four main Remark plugins created: Callouts/Blockquotes, Image Captions, Gist Partials, Video Partials
claims.quote: wrote a couple of these plugins to handle the following partials: Callouts / Blockquotes, Image Captions, Gist Partials, Video Partials

claims.claim: Old code highlighting shortcode ({{< highlight >}}) was converted to triple backticks
claims.quote: I created a script to convert the old shortcode to the new syntax

claims.claim: Author began using JSON data files for speaking sessions at beginning of 2024
claims.quote: At the beginning of 2024, I started using a JSON file to store this data

claims.claim: ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot used for data conversion, with inconsistencies requiring manual work
claims.quote: used ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot to convert the complete HTML or Markdown to a JSON list. Unfortunately, this did not work as expected. There were too many inconsistencies

claims.claim: Astro and Tailwind had breaking changes just before website launch
claims.quote: Just before putting my website live, I discovered that Astro and Tailwind had new major versions that introduced some breaking changes

claims.claim: page.body API changed to page.rendered.html in new Astro version
claims.quote: page.body → page.rendered.html in Astro

claims.claim: Tailwind config refactored from .mjs to utility-first class definitions in CSS
claims.quote: Tailwind config refactor from .mjs to utility-first class definitions in CSS

claims.quote: I use astro-expressive-code, which renders beautifully styled and readable code blocks

analysis_rows.positioning: Fast, simple, stable generator with shortcodes and partials system
analysis_rows.key_facts: Used since 2019, flawless performance, uses Go language

analysis_rows.positioning: Flexible framework with component system, JavaScript/TypeScript support, easy to get started
analysis_rows.key_facts: Supports React integration, uses .astro files, Markdown/MDX support, has breaking changes in recent versions

analysis_rows.positioning: Component-based UI library, integrates easily with Astro
analysis_rows.key_facts: Previously required webpack bundler in Hugo setup, now native integration in Astro
Had breaking changes from .mjs config to utility-first class definitions, required config refactor

analysis_rows.positioning: VS Code extension for content management
analysis_rows.key_facts: Custom tooling developed by author, integrates with decoupled content strategy
Used for data conversion, more effective in inline chat with single items than batch processing

More flexible with native React integration and component system
Stable and reliable, requires separate tooling for React

analysis_rows.symptom: 500+ blog posts needed conversion from shortcodes to components
analysis_rows.cause: Hugo and Astro have different markup systems - Hugo uses shortcodes and partials, Astro uses components
analysis_rows.evidence: Author created Remark plugins to automate conversion instead of manual updates
analysis_rows.fix: Created Remark plugins to convert: callout shortcodes to blockquotes, image captions to figure elements, Gist embeds to HTML, video embeds to HTML

analysis_rows.symptom: Old code highlighting shortcodes ({{< highlight >}}) incompatible with Astro
analysis_rows.cause: Hugo uses shortcodes, Astro expects standard Markdown triple backticks
analysis_rows.fix: Created script with regex replacement to convert all old shortcode syntax to triple backticks format

analysis_rows.symptom: Data conversion from HTML/Markdown to JSON was inconsistent and time-consuming
analysis_rows.cause: Batch processing with ChatGPT/Copilot created too many inconsistencies, required extensive manual correction
analysis_rows.evidence: Author attempted batch conversion but found too many errors requiring correction
analysis_rows.fix: Switched to inline chat with GitHub Copilot processing single items at a time for more control and consistency

analysis_rows.symptom: Breaking changes in Astro and Tailwind discovered just before site launch
analysis_rows.cause: Major version updates (Astro and Tailwind) introduced API changes
analysis_rows.evidence: page.body → page.rendered.html in Astro; Tailwind config from .mjs to utility-first CSS
analysis_rows.fix: Updated code to use new API (page.rendered.html), refactored Tailwind config to utility-first approach
